seguranca.introducao: The technical measures PathR uses to protect access to your account and the data stored in it—and what you can do on your end.
resumo: Passwords are stored only as Argon2id hashes; the plaintext password is never stored.
Login requires a verified email address, and the account is locked for 15 minutes after 5 incorrect password attempts.
Passkeys and two-factor authentication via an authenticator app are supported.
Session cookies set to `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Strict`, with rolling renewal and "log out of all devices."
Date of birth, resume, photos, and reports encrypted with AES-256-GCM within the app itself, with the key stored outside the database.
Files stored in private storage, delivered only by the server and only to those with permission.
Did you find an error? Please let privacidade@notter.com.br know before sharing it.

senhas.hashA: Passwords are stored only as hashes
senhas.hashB: , an algorithm designed to withstand attacks using graphics cards. Not even the app's operators can see your password.
itens: The password must be at least 10 characters long and include both letters and numbers—this rule is enforced on the server.
After 5 consecutive incorrect passwords, the account is locked for 15 minutes. The lock is temporary to prevent an attack from becoming a way to lock the owner out.
Invalid email addresses and incorrect passwords both receive the same message, so as not to reveal which email addresses are associated with accounts.
Only people who have confirmed their email address can sign up—that way, no one can create an account using someone else's email address.
Confirmation links (valid for 3 days) and new password links (valid for 1 hour) are single-use, and the server stores only their hashes.

fatores.passkeyResto: : You log in using biometrics or the device's PIN. The server stores only the public key, which is tied to the address pathr.notter.com.br—a fake page cannot use it. Add and remove your keys in Settings › Account.
fatores.totpResto: : When this feature is enabled, the login screen also asks for a code from an authentication app. The secret is stored in encrypted form, and the recovery codes are single-use and stored as hashes.
fatores.desafio: Each access key challenge is valid for five minutes and can only be used once.

sessao.cookiesA: The session is stored in cookies
sessao.cookiesD: (We do not process orders placed on other websites.)
itens: The access token is valid for 30 minutes. Renewal uses a second token, which is changed with each use; if a token that has already been changed reappears—a sign that it has been copied—the entire session chain is revoked.
Each request checks with the server to see if the session is still valid. Closed sessions stop working immediately, not just when they expire.
Changing your password logs you out of your other sessions; resetting your password via email logs you out of all of them.
sessao.p1b: Closes all open sessions at once.

itens: Every API endpoint requires a valid session and only returns or modifies records that belong to the logged-in user.
The browser never communicates directly with the database: only the API has the credentials, and the permissions for the database's public roles are revoked across all tables.
Resumes, profile photos, and story photos are stored privately, with no public link. They are only accessible through the server by those with permission.

Date of birth, resume (the file, the extracted text, and what the AI read from it), profile photos, and posts (message, moderator’s response, and photo) are encrypted using AES-256-GCM by the app itself before reaching the database or storage. The key is stored in the server’s secure settings, outside the database: anyone who obtains a copy of the database or the files will see only encrypted text. Each piece of data is tied to the account it belongs to, so copying it to another account won’t unlock it.
Another person's photo will only appear if they are visible in the suggestions or are connected to you.
Moderation areas appear as if they do not exist for any account other than a moderation account.
The data export does not include password hashes, two-factor authentication secrets, or session tokens.

navegador.csp: It restricts where the website loads scripts, styles, fonts, and connections from, serving as a second line of defense against code injection.
itens: The site cannot be displayed within frames on other pages (X-Frame-Options and frame-ancestors), which prevents clickjacking.
The nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy headers prevent files from being interpreted as something else or embedded by other websites.
The website blocks access to the camera, location, and browser-based payments, which the app does not use.
The interactive API documentation is disabled in production.
Resumes are accepted in PDF, DOCX, ODT, RTF, TXT, and MD formats, up to 10 MB.
Photos (profile and posts) are accepted only in JPG, PNG, or WebP format, up to 5 MB, and the file type is determined by the file size in bytes—not by the filename or what the browser reports.
A screenshot of a report is provided along with a policy that prevents any execution, even if a disguised file were to slip through the checks.
Articles from other websites displayed in the app are filtered on the server against a whitelist before they appear, and the server refuses to retrieve URLs from internal networks.
External links (articles, job postings, courses, AI responses) only become clickable if they are http or https.

limites.p1: Some resources are shared by everyone—the email quota and the artificial intelligence quota. To ensure that no one uses up what belongs to everyone, the server enforces limits:

fichas.detalhe: By IP address.
By IP, in addition to account-based blocking.
And no more than 3 per hour to the same email address.
On the house.
On the house.
On the house.
On the house.

itens: Security events—such as registration, logins, errors, and two-factor authentication—are logged with the date, IP address, and browser. The log never contains passwords, codes, or tokens.
Server errors are logged without any emails, identifiers, or tokens in the message.
A daily automated review checks for errors, reports, and project dependencies, and the moderation team receives a summary via email.
Use a password that you don't use anywhere else, or a password manager.
Register an access key for your device in Settings › Account.
If you suspect that someone has accessed your account, change your password and use “Sign out of all devices.”
Be wary of messages asking for your password: PathR never asks for your password via email. If in doubt, type pathr.notter.com.br directly into your browser instead of clicking on a link.
On shared computers, log out of your account when you're done—this also deletes the offline copy saved in the browser.

vulnerabilidades.p1b: with a description of the problem and the steps to reproduce it. We ask that you do not access, alter, or delete other people’s data, do not disrupt the service, and allow a reasonable amount of time for the issue to be fixed before making it public. PathR does not have a bug bounty program, but we appreciate your reports—and we respond.
